title: Wix Pricing 2026: Every Plan, Its Price and Its Limits
summary: Wix pricing spans free to $50+ monthly across six tiers. Compare costs, features, and restrictions for each to select the plan matching your needs.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Wix costs and limits that surprise buyers


### Wix domain, app and renewal costs


A plan's monthly price covers the site, not everything around it. A domain is billed on its own renewal cycle, so the year-one offer isn't your year-two cost.


Three apps at modest prices can outweigh the jump between two plan tiers, because each paid app from the Wix App Market adds its own subscription.


### Payment fees and ecommerce limits


**Wix Payments fees follow the payment method, not the plan, so upgrading a tier doesn't make a card sale cheaper.**


An in-person sale on Wix POS costs[2.6% of the transaction](https://support.wix.com/en/article/wix-payments-transaction-fees) , which is the lowest rate, and a standard card or debit payment costs 2.9%.


> **Wix Payments fees follow the payment method, not the plan, so upgrading a tier doesn't make a card sale cheaper.


PayPal costs 3.49%, and American Express costs 3.7%, **making Amex the more expensive payment option** , so merchants accept less revenue per transaction when customers choose Amex.


On $10,000 of monthly sales, that spread is $260 in person against $370 on American Express, a $110 difference. If many of your customers pay with Amex, that gap is a recurring cost no plan removes.


### Wix storage, bandwidth and collaborator limits


Once a media-heavy site such as a portfolio, course library or video-led store fills its allowance, the storage and bandwidth ceiling is the first one it hits, and each plan carries its own.


Hitting a cap usually means moving up a tier, so **a cheap plan turns into the next one** without your having chosen it.


Every person you add, such as a bookkeeper or developer, takes a collaborator seat, and each seat has to fit the plan's allowance.


### Connecting Wix to other business tools


Costs creep in again when you move orders or form submissions into a spreadsheet, CRM or email tool. Automation tools bill by the task, meaning one action in a workflow.


Activepieces is one option for multi-step workflows beyond Wix's built-in automations. Its published pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, however many steps the flow contains, whereas Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's bills per module.


The free plan includes 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows.


So a store that sends every order through several steps spends one credit per order rather than one per step, and 1,000 credits cover 1,000 orders. On per-task billing the same flow would use up that allowance several times faster.
